foundations.purpose: Lean 4.33.1 logical and datatype foundations; kernel checks proof terms.
Extensional predicate sets, membership, subset, images and set algebra.
Ordinary/generalized syntax, occurrence predicates and blank-node transports, including generated eliminators and equality decisions.
Subtype domains, partial assignments, restriction and denotation agreement proofs.
Truth-preservation composition and explicit witness/countermodel constructions.
Transport along blank-node functions and disjoint-union assignments.
Engineering contract for finite enumerations: exact set membership plus no duplicate occurrences. Not a W3C claim that every graph is finite.
Small formal counterexample exhibiting the informative shared-witness issue.
Draft structural range and record-reference certificate implementing COV-01/02/03; not a semantic completeness proof.
Checked countermodel to an unrestricted generalized-graph reading; source scope remains an explicit expert-review question, not an asserted erratum.
Simultaneous term substitution, resource-valued pullbacks and inverse renaming on occurring blanks; generated helpers inherit these obligations.
Canonical interpretation, assignment decoding and ordinary interpolation, including generated helpers.
Finite image enumeration and compactness through interpolation.
Syntactic name occurrence including the explicit literal datatype projection.
Name preservation by substitution and nonexpansion under simple entailment.
Scoped freshness, inverse-name retraction and conservativity over the existing substitution and entailment definitions.
Model existence, process truth preservation and composition under semantic extensions.
A single RDF property condition, its rule consequence and conditional generalized substitution theorem; not a complete RDF interpretation.
Bridge typed IEXT, ambient relation notation and triple denotations.
Fixed datatype theory, partial value realization, D-conditions and model-class proofs; concrete datatype meanings remain external.
Symbolic RDF vocabulary, complete infinite axiom family, RDF-condition conjunction and its consequences.
Shared fresh witness for rdfD1 and inherited datatype inconsistency.
RDFS vocabulary, axiom families, class-extension definitions and semantic conditions in one shared universe.
RDFS rule instances, compositional truth/entailment soundness and derived disjoint-datatype inconsistency.
Construct explicit D-models, characterize satisfiability, and exhibit a conditional entailment-direction counterexample.
Recognized literal values and simultaneous value-preserving graph substitution.
Source-exact generalized axiom seeds, inductive closure and positive-check soundness; completeness remains open.
Derive generic membership from indexed membership through full RDFS axioms and named rules.
Ordinary dataset syntax, equivalence with unique-name pairs, global occurrence support and presence-sensitive representation equality.
Global blank bijections preserving default and named graphs, with induced component graph isomorphisms and equivalence.
Checked witnesses for loss of cross-graph sharing and loss of empty-named-graph presence under quad projection.
Explicit candidate dataset regimes, adopted content conditions, model restrictions and conditional graph-consequence transfer.
A fixed-IRI presence policy retains default content and isomorphism invariance while changing dataset entailment.
Two explicit simple-model witnesses with true component graphs and an example graph-object embedding; RDF/RDFS and engine guidance remain separate.
Illustrative fixed-name graph comparisons with empty fallback, and a checked distinction from structural dataset isomorphism.

Explicit full-domain RDF model construction, reuse of D-model literals, sufficient parameter assumptions and countermodels for non-type ground assertions. These choices do not redefine the RDF model class.

Necessary compatibility consequences from the existing RDF/RDFS conditions: actual language-literal representatives and transfer of unsatisfiability through model inclusion. Not a model-existence assumption.

Explicit RDFS witness family over the existing RDF model, full condition and axiom proofs, language-literal coverage equivalence for base D, and source-facing countermodels. Constructor choices do not redefine RDFS interpretations.

declarations.name: RDF11.GeneralizedScope.I._proof_2
declarations.type: true = false ∨ true = true

declarations.name: RDF11.GeneralizedScope.I._proof_3
declarations.type: false = false ∨ false = true

declarations.name: RDF11.GeneralizedScope.I.eq_1
declarations.type:
∀ {Iri Literal : Type} [inst : DecidableEq Iri] (p : Iri),
  RDF11.GeneralizedScope.I p =
    { IR := fun x => x = false, IR_nonempty := RDF11.GeneralizedScope.I._proof_1, IP := fun x => x = true,
      IEXT := fun x x_1 => True,
      IS := fun i =>
        if i = p then ⟨true, RDF11.GeneralizedScope.I._proof_2⟩ else ⟨false, RDF11.GeneralizedScope.I._proof_3⟩,
      IL := fun x => none }

declarations.name: RDF11.DatatypeModel.interpretation.eq_1
declarations.type:
∀ {Iri Literal Value : Type} (T : RDF11.DatatypeTheory Iri Literal Value) (D : RDF11.Set Iri),
  RDF11.DatatypeModel.interpretation T D =
    { IR := fun x => True, IR_nonempty := ⋯, IP := fun x => True, IEXT := fun x x_1 => True,
      IS := fun a => ⟨if D a then RDF11.DatatypeModel.embed (T.identified a) else RDF11.DatatypeModel.unnamed, ⋯⟩,
      IL := fun l => Option.map (fun x => ⟨x, True.intro⟩) (RDF11.DatatypeModel.literal T D l) }

declarations.name: RDF11.DatatypeModel.literal
declarations.type:
{Iri Literal Value : Type} →
  RDF11.DatatypeTheory Iri Literal Value → RDF11.Set Iri → Literal → Option (RDF11.DatatypeModel.Carrier Value)

declarations.name: RDF11.DatatypeModel.literal.eq_1
declarations.type:
∀ {Iri Literal Value : Type} (T : RDF11.DatatypeTheory Iri Literal Value) (D : RDF11.Set Iri) (l : Literal),
  RDF11.DatatypeModel.literal T D l =
    if D (T.literalSyntax.datatype l) then
      match T.literalSyntax.language l with
      | some tag =>
        some (RDF11.DatatypeModel.embed (T.languageValue (T.literalSyntax.lexical l) (RDF11.asciiLower tag)))
      | none =>
        Option.map RDF11.DatatypeModel.embed
          (T.L2V (T.identified (T.literalSyntax.datatype l)) (T.literalSyntax.lexical l))
    else some RDF11.DatatypeModel.unnamed

declarations.name: RDF11.DatatypeTheory.RecognizedValue.casesOn
declarations.type:
∀ {Iri Literal Value : Type} {T : RDF11.DatatypeTheory Iri Literal Value} {D : RDF11.Set Iri} {a : Literal}
  {motive : (a_1 : Value) → T.RecognizedValue D a a_1 → Prop} {a_1 : Value} (t : T.RecognizedValue D a a_1),
  (∀ (tag : String) (a_2 : D T.literalSyntax.langString) (a_3 : T.literalSyntax.language a = some tag),
      motive (T.languageValue (T.literalSyntax.lexical a) (RDF11.asciiLower tag)) ⋯) →
    (∀ (a_2 : Iri) (v : Value) (a_3 : D a_2) (a_4 : a_2 ≠ T.literalSyntax.langString)
        (a_5 : T.literalSyntax.datatype a = a_2) (a_6 : T.L2V (T.identified a_2) (T.literalSyntax.lexical a) = some v),
        motive v ⋯) →
      motive a_1 t

  (tag : String),
  D T.literalSyntax.langString →
    T.literalSyntax.language l = some tag →
      T.RecognizedValue D l (T.languageValue (T.literalSyntax.lexical l) (RDF11.asciiLower tag))

declarations.name: RDF11.DatatypeTheory.RecognizedValue.ordinary

  D a →
    a ≠ T.literalSyntax.langString →
      T.literalSyntax.datatype l = a →
        T.L2V (T.identified a) (T.literalSyntax.lexical l) = some v → T.RecognizedValue D l v

  {motive : (a_1 : Value) → T.RecognizedValue D a a_1 → Prop},
  (∀ (tag : String) (a_1 : D T.literalSyntax.langString) (a_2 : T.literalSyntax.language a = some tag),
      motive (T.languageValue (T.literalSyntax.lexical a) (RDF11.asciiLower tag)) ⋯) →
    (∀ (a_1 : Iri) (v : Value) (a_2 : D a_1) (a_3 : a_1 ≠ T.literalSyntax.langString)
        (a_4 : T.literalSyntax.datatype a = a_1) (a_5 : T.L2V (T.identified a_1) (T.literalSyntax.lexical a) = some v),
        motive v ⋯) →
      ∀ {a_1 : Value} (t : T.RecognizedValue D a a_1), motive a_1 t

declarations.name: RDF11.DatatypeTheory.RecognizedValue.recOn
declarations.type:
∀ {Iri Literal Value : Type} {T : RDF11.DatatypeTheory Iri Literal Value} {D : RDF11.Set Iri} {a : Literal}

  (∀ (tag : String) (a_2 : D T.literalSyntax.langString) (a_3 : T.literalSyntax.language a = some tag),

declarations.name: RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.interpretation.eq_1
declarations.type:
∀ {Iri Literal Value : Type} (T : RDF11.DatatypeTheory Iri Literal Value) (D : RDF11.Set Iri)
  (v : RDF11.RDFVocabulary Iri)
  (R :
    RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.Carrier Iri Value →
      RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.Carrier Iri Value → RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.Carrier Iri Value → Prop),
  RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.interpretation T D v R =
    { IR := fun x => True, IR_nonempty := ⋯, IP := fun x => True,
      IEXT := fun p xy =>
        if p.val = RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.name (v.iri RDF11.RDFSymbol.rdfType) then
          RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.typeExtension T xy.fst.val xy.snd.val
        else R p.val xy.fst.val xy.snd.val,
      IS := fun a => ⟨RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.iriValue T D a, ⋯⟩,
      IL := fun l =>
        Option.map (fun r => ⟨RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.lift r.val, True.intro⟩)
          ((RDF11.DatatypeModel.interpretation T D).IL l) }

  (v : RDF11.RDFVocabulary Iri)
  (R :

  ¬D p →
    p ≠ v.iri RDF11.RDFSymbol.rdfType →
      ((RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.interpretation T D v R).TripleTrue A
          { subject := RDF11.Term.iri s, predicate := RDF11.Term.iri p, object := RDF11.Term.iri o } ↔
        R (RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.name p) (RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.iriValue T D s)

    ∀ (s p o : Iri),
      ¬D p →
        p ≠ v.iri RDF11.RDFSymbol.rdfType →
          have G :=
            RDF11.Set.singleton
              { subject := RDF11.Term.iri s, predicate := RDF11.Term.iri p, object := RDF11.Term.iri o };

RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.relates_iff
declarations.type:
∀ {Iri Literal Value : Type} (T : RDF11.DatatypeTheory Iri Literal Value) (D : RDF11.Set Iri)
  (v : RDF11.RDFVocabulary Iri)

    if p = RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.name (v.iri RDF11.RDFSymbol.rdfType) then

declarations.type:

                object := RDF11.Term.iri (v.iri RDF11.RDFSSymbol.resource) };
